source.author: hor
source.text: Integer vitae scelerisque purus non eget Mauris iaculis neque arcu nec venenatis gravida sagittis, Fusce, pharetra, sive per Syrtis iter aestuosas sive facturus per inhospitalem Caucasum vel quae loca fabulosus lambit Hydaspes.
source.text_original: Integer vitae scelerisque purus / non eget Mauris iaculis neque arcu / nec venenatis gravida sagittis, / Fusce, pharetra, / sive per Syrtis iter aestuosas / sive facturus per inhospitalem / Caucasum vel quae loca fabulosus / lambit Hydaspes.
source.text_english: The man of upright life and free from wickedness has no need of Moorish javelins, nor of bows or arrows laden with poison, Fusce, whether he is to make his way through the burning Syrtes or through inhospitable Caucasus, or whatever places the fabled Hydaspes skirts.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: recte igitur Flaccus tantam esse dixit innocentiae uim, ut ad tutelam sui non egeat nec armis nec uiribus, quacumque iter fecerit: integer uitae scelerisque purus non eget Mauris iaculis nec arcu nec uenenatis grauida sagittis, Fusce, pharetra, siue per Syrtis iter aestuosas siue facturus per inhospitalem Caucasum uel quae loca fabulosus lambit Hydaspes.
reuse.text_original: recte igitur Flaccus tantam esse dixit innocentiae uim, ut ad tutelam sui non egeat nec armis nec uiribus, quacumque iter fecerit: integer uitae scelerisque purus non eget Mauris iaculis nec arcu nec uenenatis grauida sagittis, Fusce, pharetra, siue per Syrtis iter aestuosas siue facturus per inhospitalem Caucasum uel quae loca fabulosus lambit Hydaspes.
reuse.text_english: Therefore Flaccus rightly said that innocence has such great power that, wherever it travels, it does not need either weapons or strength for its own protection: one who is pure in life and free from wrongdoing needs neither Moorish spears nor a bow nor a quiver heavy with poisoned arrows, Fusce, whether he is to travel through the burning Syrtes or through inhospitable Caucasus or the lands which the fabulous Hydaspes licks along its course.
